trace_steps: frame_retriever returns the puzzle screen at 9.0s, 13.5s, and 19.5s, with frame_9.00.png the strongest candidate (relevance_score 0.7262). OCR across these frames reads the four tray labels as "70 ₹", "30 ₹", "60 ₹", and "?" with avg detection confidence 0.9465, so the task is to infer the missing price from the other three trays.

In frame_9.00.png, spatial_grounder marks two fruit items on the top-left tray with bboxes [192, 362, 310, 452] and [288, 322, 420, 412] (confidences 0.98 and 0.97), two fruit items on the top-right tray with bboxes [488, 357, 610, 447] and [584, 347, 720, 437] (0.96 and 0.95), and two fruit items on the bottom-left tray with bboxes [142, 607, 260, 697] and [242, 567, 370, 657] (0.97 and 0.96). However, the tool labels all of them only as generic "fruit on tray" rather than identifying which are mangoes, apples, or oranges.

The last tray is also visible: spatial_grounder on frame_19.50.png detects two fruit items on the bottom-right tray at [465, 612, 578, 692] and [578, 632, 728, 702] with confidences 0.97 and 0.96, and OCR reads the nearby label as "?". But because the fruit identities on all trays were not resolved beyond generic detections, there is no grounded way to form the three fruit-value equations needed to solve the final tray price.
Therefore the tool evidence is insufficient to determine a unique numeric total for the last tray, so the correct choice is D: There is insufficient information to solve the problem.
